title: Borrowed Parts
logline: Over several visits to a limb-fitting workshop, a newly made leg goes from a cast to a first careful walk, and the words its wearer uses for it change along the way.
human_question: At what point does something made by other hands become 'my leg'?

situation.what_happens: A person is measured and cast for a prosthesis, a socket is shaped and ground, and over several visits it is fitted, walked on, found uncomfortable, adjusted and walked on again. Weeks later it is either in daily use or it is not.
situation.who_is_involved: The wearer; the technicians who make and adjust the limb; the household and workplace the wearer returns to.
situation.what_is_at_stake: Mobility, work, independence and cost, on the wearer's own terms and in the wearer's own words.
situation.how_it_unfolds: Fittings run over weeks and the outcome is not known in advance: some limbs are used daily, some are used rarely, and the reasons are practical rather than inspirational.

concept_merge.why_together: None survives review. The proposed merge rested on treating a fitted limb as a test case for 'clung-to' matter, and the C067 digest does not support that reading: clung-to matter there names a psychological grip that the sources apply to the eighteen kamma-born kinds, and it is explicitly not a claim about bodily ownership or autonomy. No other link in the group's concept set carries this situation without importing what the digests forbid.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Nothing that survives the philosophy check. The record is kept so that the reasoning is not lost, not as a proposal.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Nothing is proposed. The idea is not carried forward in this group.
what_must_be_real: Not applicable: the idea is dropped. Were any related situation ever revisited, the wearer's own story, pace and language would have to lead it entirely, and no doctrinal account of bodies or faculties could be offered to them or laid over them.
position_hint: none: dropped at review, so no position is proposed.
risks: Using a disabled participant as the vehicle for a doctrine that the digests forbid applying to any real person's body.
A triumph-over-adversity arc imposed from outside.

connections.note: The group's work on what is held as 'mine' is carried by IDEA-0124, where the sources' own examples, the sense organs, are the subject.

selection.reason: The primary link misreads the source: the C067 digest defines clung-to matter as a psychological grip applying especially to the eighteen kamma-born kinds, and says explicitly that it is not a claim about owning a body, so a manufactured limb cannot be an instance of it. Beyond the misreading, the situation would place a disabled participant inside a doctrinal frame that the C064, C068, C069 and C071 digests all forbid applying to any real person's body or faculties. Nothing from it is folded into a kept idea.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
